אם הוא בידו. ל' הטור כגון שנתנו בידו לשומרו ור"ל דל"ת דבידו היינו בידו לנסכו אלא דהיינו שנתנו בידו לשומרו והוי כבעליו עליו ולא מטעם מיגו וכ"פ הרא"ש פ' הנזקין בחילוק י"א והמרדכי ר"פ האשה רבה אבל הב"י לא הביא דברי הרא"ש ומרדכי אלו ואדרבה הביא בסתם דברי רש"י ור"ת והרשב"א שפירשו כל שבידו לטמא ואולי לזה השמיט כאן ל' הטור וכן בעט"ז פי' הטעם משום שישנו בידו לחסרו וכן הוכיח הרשב"א בחידושיו פרק הנזקין ריש דף ע"ט בראיות וכן משמע בתו' בקדושין פרק האומר (דף ס"ה ע"ב) דמהימן משום מגו ועפ"ז יש לדון במי שאומר לחבירו על יין מבושל שלו שנתנסך קודם הבישול אינו נאמן) אפי' הוא בידו כיון דלית ליה מגו:
נאמן. אפילו לא אמר ליה בפעם הראשון שמצאו:
אם בפעם כו' אפילו הבעל דין מכחישו. באמת זאת היא דעת התוספות והרא"ש ומרדכי ושאר הרבה פוסקים אבל קשה דהא כללא הוא לא יקום עד אחד באיש וגו' דעד א' אינו קם רק לשבועה ונהי דקי"ל עד א' נאמן באיסורים היינו היכא דאין הבע"ד מכחישו או במקום דאיכא מגו אבל במקום דליכא לא הא ולא הא לא מיסתבר כלל דעד א' יהא נאמן להכחיש הבע"ד ולהפסיד ממונו ואף בדאיכא מגו ק"ק דהא כתבו הרא"ש והט"ו בח"מ סימן ק"ח סי"ד דאינו נאמן (וכה"ג הקשו התוס' בעשרה יוחסין והרא"ש פ"ק דמציעא ושאר פוסקים אמ"ש רש"י דהיכא דאין מקחו בידו נאמן לומר לזה מכרתי אי נקט זוזי מחד דאמאי יהא נאמן טפי מעובד כוכבים דעלמא עכ"ד אע"ג דהיה בידו מתחלה) אלא דיש לחלק קצת ע"ש והשטה המחוורת בש"ס היא שטת הראב"ד והרשב"א דמפרשים הך דאמרינן בהנזקין דאי אשכחי' וא"ל מיד נאמן בשותק ומחלקין בין פועל דגרע מעד דעלמא ע"ש וכ"כ הר"ן בהנזקין והיא שטת האחרונים שהביא הר"ן פרק האומר וזהו דעת הרמב"ם סוף הלכות פסולי המוקדשין וסוף ה' מטמאי משכב ומושב דדוקא בשותק נאמן ע"ש ודו"ק: **** ENGLISH **** If for the first time, etc., even if the owner of the wine contradicts him. In truth this is the view of Tosafot, the Rosh, Mordechai, and many other poskim; but it is difficult, for the principle is "one witness shall not rise against a man," and a single witness stands only for an oath; and although we hold one witness is believed in prohibitions, that is where the owner of the wine does not contradict him, or where there is a migu; but where there is neither this nor that, it is not reasonable at all that one witness should be believed to contradict the owner of the wine and cause him monetary loss; and even where there is a migu it is difficult, for the Rosh and Tur in Choshen Mishpat siman 108 seif 14 wrote that he is not believed (and similarly Tosafot challenged in Yuchasin, the Rosh in the first chapter of Bava Metzia, and other poskim, as Rashi explained: where the purchase is not in his hand he is believed to say "I sold to this one" if he took payment from one — why should he be more believed than an ordinary gentile? — end of his words, even though it was in his hand initially); but one may distinguish somewhat — see there; and the correct approach in the Gemara is the view of the Raavad and Rashba, who explain the case in Nezikin that if we find him and he says immediately he is believed in silence, and they distinguish between a worker, who is inferior to an ordinary witness — see there; and likewise the Ran in Nezikin; and it is the view of the Acharonim that the Ran brought in the chapter HaOmer; and this is the view of the Rambam at the end of Hilchot Pesulei HaMukdashin and at the end of Hilchot Metamei Mishkav uMoshav, that specifically in silence he is believed — see there, and examine carefully.
נאמן. כתב הרב בתשוב' סי' ס"ו דאם הבעל מכחישו ואמר שלא א"ל בפעם הראשון ודאי הבעל נאמן ועיין עוד שם מדינים אלו: **** ENGLISH **** Believed. The rabbi wrote in his responsum siman 66 that if the owner contradicts him and says he did not tell him the first time, certainly the owner is believed; and see further there these laws.
אבל אם אינו בידו. פי' אפי' היה בידו מתחלה מ"מ כיון שאינו עתה בידו ולא א"ל בפעם הא' אינו נאמן אבל כשלא היה בידו מעולם אפי' א"ל בפעם הא' אינו נאמן כשהבע"ד מכחישו אלא בששותק כן מבואר בתוספות והרא"ש ומרדכי וסייעתו והמחבר קיצר בדבר:
אם הבעל מכחישו. ואז מותר לכל העולם וכן כתב הרב בסוף הסעיף ואפילו אמר איני יודע מותר לכל העולם כמ"ש כאו"ה כלל י"ג די"ג בשם ר"ח וכ"פ בד"מ:
או אומר כו'. כתוב במרדכי פ' האומר דאם א"ל שמא לא דקדקת חשיב כאלו מכחישו ומביאו בד"מ:
אינו יודע. ע"ל ס"ק ט"ו:
אבל אם שתק כו'. פי' אפי' אחר שלא היה בידו מעולם ולא א"ל בפעם הא' לעולם כיון דשתק כהודאה דמיא וז"ל הטור אבל אחר שאינו בידו או שלא אמ"ל השומר לבעליו בפעם הא' וא"ל אח"כ אינו נאמן ודוקא שהבעלים מכחישין אותו או אומר אינו יודע אבל אם שותק שתיקה כהודאה דמיא עכ"ל וכתב הב"ח ונראה לי מלשון הטור מדכתב אבל אחר שאינו בידו או שלא אמר השומר כו' ולא כתב או שלא אמר בפעם הא' אלמא משמע דבאחר שאינו שומר שלא היה בידו אין חילוק בין בפעם הא' לפעם הב' לעולם אם שותק כהודאה דמיא וכ"כ ב"י ע"ש הרשב"א בחידושיו כו' עכ"ל ותימא גדולה דהא גבי הכחשה הוא דכתב הטור או שלא אמר השומר כו' אבל בסיפא גבי שתיקה לא חילק ועוד שהרי עומד בשטת התוס' והרא"ש וסייעתם והם הקשו מהא דאביי דאמר עד אחד נאמן כששותק אע"ג שלא היה בידו מעולם אהך דהנזקין דאמר אביי גבי שומר דאם אינו בידו אינו נאמן ויישבו בדוחק ואם איתא הא אין התחלה לקושיא זו אלא אדרבה סברת התוס' והרא"ש היא להדיא הפוכה מסברת הרשב"א וס"ל דשומר עדיף מעד דעלמא כיון שהיה פעם אחד בידו והכי משמע נמי להדיא ממ"ש הרא"ש ואדרבה נמי קשה דאע"ג דמהימן ליה כו' ע"ש והכי מוכח נמי להדיא במרדכי פ' האומר גבי מ"ש שם וכתב ראבי"ה רבא נמי מודה באין בידו ושותק כדמשמע הכא כו' דגבי שומר שהיה בידו נמי אמרינן דשתיקה הוי הודאה אפי' בפעם ב' וע"ק דכיון דאמרינן שתיקה כהודאה דמיא מה חילוק בין שומר או עד דעלמא הא כל שא"ל בפניך נתנסך או ידעת רגלים לדבר ה"ל להשיבו ומדשתק הודה וא"כ אין חילוק וכך הקשה בד"מ על הרשב"א ומביאו הדרישה אלא דהד"מ לא הקשה כלום אהרשב"א דאיהו אזיל לטעמיה דס"ל בתשובה סימן שע"ו דהא דקאמר אביי שותק נאמן לאו משום דשתיקה כהודאה היא ואצ"ל בפניך וכה"ג אלא אפי' שותק מפני שאינו יודע בירור הדבר נאמן וכמ"ש בס"ק ט"ו בשמו ולכך מחלק בין שומר לאחר דשומר לא מהימן כולי האי דחזקת מיזהר זהיר כיון דעליה רמיא מילתא כו' אבל להטור דס"ל שתיקה כהודאה דמיא ודאי דאין חילוק אלא ודאי כך הוי פשט הטור אבל אחר שאינו בידו כלומר שלא היה בידו מעולם אפילו אמר ליה מיד אינו נאמן כל שהבעל מכחישו או אפי' שומר שהיה בידו אם לא א"ל בפעם הא' אינו נאמן כשמכחישו או אומר איני יודע אבל אם שותק אין חילוק בין אחר לשומר בין א"ל מיד או לא לעולם שתיקה כהודאה דמיא וכך הם דברי המחבר וכן מבואר בתוס' והרא"ש וסייעתם ונראה דהוי שותק בענין דודאי שתיקתו הודאה כגון דא"ל בפניך וכה"ג גם הרשב"א מודה דאין חילוק בין שומר לאחר בין א"ל מיד או לא לעולם נאמן וכל זה ברור: **** ENGLISH **** But if he was silent, etc. Meaning: even after it was never in his hand and he never told him the first time, since he was silent it is like admission; and such is the language of the Tur: but afterward, when it is not in his hand, or the guardian did not tell the owner the first time and afterward told him, he is not believed — and specifically when the owners contradict him or say they do not know; but if they are silent, silence is like admission — end of his words; and Bach wrote: it appears to me from the Tur's language, since he wrote "but afterward when it is not in his hand, or the guardian did not say," and did not write "or did not say the first time," it implies that afterward, when he is no longer the guardian and it was not in his hand, there is no distinction between the first time and the second time forever — if he is silent, silence is like admission; and likewise Beit Yosef there, Rashba in his chiddushim, etc. — end of his words; and one may raise a great astonishment, for regarding contradiction the Tur wrote "or the guardian did not say," but in the latter part regarding silence he did not distinguish; and further, behold he follows the view of Tosafot, the Rosh, and their supporters, and they challenged from that which Abaye said that a silent witness is believed even though it was never in his hand, against that which is in Nezikin regarding a guardian that if it is not in his hand he is not believed; and they resolved with difficulty; and if so, there is no beginning to this question — rather, on the contrary, the view of Tosafot and the Rosh is explicitly the opposite of Rashba's view, and they hold that a guardian is superior to an ordinary witness since it was once in his hand; and such appears explicitly from the Rosh's words; and on the contrary it is also difficult, for even though he is believed to him, etc. — see there; and such is proven explicitly in Mordechai in the chapter HaOmer regarding what is written there, and Rabbenu Yehuda wrote: Rava too agrees when it is not in his hand and he is silent, as appears here, etc., that regarding a guardian who was in his hand we also say silence is admission even the second time; and one may challenge: since we say silence is like admission, what difference between a guardian or an ordinary witness — for whoever was told "it was libated in your presence" or "you knew circumstantial evidence" should have answered him, and since he was silent he admitted; if so there is no distinction; and thus Darkei Moshe challenged Rashba, and he brings it Derishah; except Darkei Moshe did not challenge Rashba at all, for he follows his reasoning that that which Abaye says a silent witness is believed is not because silence is admission, and all the more "in your presence," and similarly; rather, even if he is silent because he does not know the matter clearly, he is believed, as written in s.k. 15 in his name; and therefore he distinguishes between a guardian and others, for a guardian is not so believed because he is presumed to be very careful since the matter rests upon him, etc.; but according to the Tur, who holds silence is like admission, certainly there is no distinction; but when it was never in his hand, even if he told him immediately, he is not believed as long as the owner contradicts him; or a guardian who was in his hand, if he did not tell him the first time, he is not believed when they contradict him or say they do not know; but if they are silent, there is no distinction between others and a guardian, whether he told him immediately or not forever — silence is like admission; and such are the words of the Mechaber, and so it is explained in Tosafot, the Rosh, and their supporters; and it appears this is silence in a matter where certainly his silence is admission, such as where he was told "in your presence," and similarly; Rashba too agrees there is no distinction between a guardian and others, whether he told him immediately or not — he is believed; and all this is clear.
שתיקה כהודאה דמיא. לאו כהודאה ממש דא"כ פשיטא וגם לא היינו צריכים לנאמנות העד ועוד דמוכח בפרק האומר (דף ס"ו ע"א) דאם היה העד גזלן אפילו שותק אינו נאמן אלא כיון ששותק נראה שיודע רגלים לדבר וסומך על העד כ"כ התוס' ר"פ האשה רבה וכ"כ התוס' פרק האומר שם ד"ה רבא והמרדכי לשם וצ"ע אהר"ן שדחק ליישב דברי התו' במ"ש דשתיקה כהודאה דמיא ונעלם ממנו דברי התוס' אלו ע"ש: **** ENGLISH **** Silence is like admission. Not literally like admission, for then it would be obvious, and we would not need the witness's credibility; and further, it is proven in the chapter HaOmer (daf 66 side 1) that if the witness was a robber, even if he is silent he is not believed; rather, since he is silent it appears he knows circumstantial evidence and relies on the witness — so wrote Tosafot in the first chapter of HaIsha Rabba, and likewise Tosafot in the chapter HaOmer there s.v. Rava, and Mordechai there; and it is difficult on the Ran, who forced himself to resolve the words of Tosafot with what is written that silence is like admission, and these words of Tosafot were hidden from him — see there.
ומלמדין אותו כו'. פי' מלמדים אותו קודם שא"ל העד שכשיבא העד ויאמר לו יאמר לו מיד תוך כדי דיבור איני מאמינך ואין מלמדין אותו להכחישו דהיאך ילמדוהו לשקר:
אע"פ שמכחישו אחר לא מהני. מה שהוציא זה בד"מ מהגמי"י פי"א ונרשם כן בש"ע לא מצאתי בהגהמי"י שלפני אבל האו"ה כלל י"ג דין י"ג כ"כ בשם הסמ"ג (והוא בס"ס רכ"ג) אבל צל"ע בדין זה דהא אביי דקאמר בש"ס א"ל עד א' והלה שותק נאמן יליף ליה ממאי דתנן בכריתות ר"פ אמרו לו א"ל עד א' אכלת חלב והלה אומר לא אכלתי פטור טעמא דאמר הא אישתיק מהימן ובריש ההיא מתני' תנן א"ל עד א' אכל ועד א' אמר לא אכל מביא אשם תלוי וע"כ בששותק (מחמת הודאה כגון שא"ל היה לך לידע וכמ"ש בספרי ע"ש) דאי מכחישו פשיטא וכ"ש מסיפא דפטור דאפ"ה מהני הכחשת העד דאמר לא אכל לפוטרו מוודאי קרבן אלמא אע"ג דשתיק לא אמרינן דהודה להאי דאמר אכל דאע"ג דלשטה זו דהתוס' והרא"ש והטור וסייעתם טעמא דשותק מהימן משום דכיון ששותק נראה שיודע קצת רגלים לדבר ומודה קצת לדברי העד וסומך עליו מכל מקום כיון דע"א מכחישו י"ל דסומך אהמכחיש א"נ דיודע קצת רגלים לזה ולזה ואע"ג דהיכא דשותק מפני שאינו יודע בירור הדבר אינו נאמן שאני התם דלא הוי עדות העד כלל דבעינן שיודה לו הבע"ד קצת א"נ שאני חלבים שכן אפי' אמר לבו נוקפו מביא אשם תלוי וכמ"ש בס"ק י"ג בשם הירושלמי ע"ש מ"מ מוכח דאע"ג דהבעלים שם ושותקים מהני הכחשת העד ודוחק לומר דהא דקאמר לא מהני היינו לענין שיהא היין מותר בודאי אלא מידי ספיקא לא נפקא אבל אין ה"נ דאינו אסור בודאי דהא אית' בסמ"ק ס"ס רכ"ג ובאו"ה שם ובד"מ בשם הגהמי"י דהכחשת העד דאומר לא נתנסך לא מהני אפילו להתירו לעצמו ואם איתא דספיקא הוא אמאי לא יהא מותר להעד עצמו והא אפי' באשת איש קי"ל דאם עד אחד אומר מת בעלה ועד אחד אומר לא מת אם נישאת לאותו שאומר מת אע"ג דכל פעם שבא עליה באשם תלוי קאי לא תצא כמ"ש הרמב"ם פי"ב מהלכות גירושין דין י"ט וכמו שהוכיח ה' המגיד לשם בראיה ברורה מן הירושלמי וראיות אחרות ג"כ ואף להרמב"ן והרא"ש בתשובה דפליגי התם היינו מטעמא כיון דהיא בחזקת א"א אוקי גברא להדי גברא ואוקי אתתא בחזקת א"א כדמוכח לשם משא"כ הכא ודוק וצ"ל לסמ"ק ואו"ה דמ"מ איסורא איכא לכתחלה ולפ"ז בדיעבד אין להחמיר להעד עצמו: **** ENGLISH **** Even though another contradicts him, it does not help. That which Darkei Moshe brought from the Gemara in the first chapter and was written thus in Shulchan Aruch — I did not find it in the hagahot before him; but Or Zarua general law 13 likewise wrote so in the name of Semag (and it is at the end of siman 223); but one may be astonished at this law, for Abaye who says in the Gemara "one witness told him and the other is silent — he is believed" learned it from what we taught in Keritot in the first chapter: they told him, he told one witness "you ate forbidden fat," and the other says "I did not eat" — he is exempt; the reason is that he said "behold he was silent" — he is believed; and at the beginning of that mishnah we taught: one witness says he ate and one witness says he did not eat — he brings a conditional guilt offering; and it must be when he is silent (due to admission, such as where they told him "you should have known," as written in the Sifrei — see there); for if they contradict him it is obvious; and all the more from the end that he is exempt — that even so the contradiction of the witness who says "he did not eat" to exempt him from a definite sacrifice proves that even though he was silent we do not say he admitted to this one who says "he ate"; nevertheless, since one witness contradicts him, one may say he relies on the contradictor, or he knows circumstantial evidence for this one and for that one; and even though where he is silent because he does not know the matter clearly he is not believed — that is different there, for the witness's testimony is not valid at all, for we require that the owner of the wine admit somewhat to him; or chelev is different, for there even if his heart tells him he brings a conditional guilt offering, as written in s.k. 13 in the name of the Yerushalmi — see there; nevertheless it is proven that even though the owners are there and silent, the contradiction of the witness helps; and it is strained to say that that which he says "it does not help" is only so the wine should be permitted with certainty, but it does not emerge from doubt; but it is not so, for it is in Semak siman 223 and Or Zarua there and Darkei Moshe in the name of the hagahot that the contradiction of the witness who says "it was not libated" does not help even to permit it to himself; and if it is a doubt, why should it not be permitted to the witness himself? Rather the matter is clear that such is the thrust of his words: "One witness contradicting the owner of the wine is nothing, as is in the end of the chapter HaOmer," which challenges there "and is it reasonable — is one witness in contradiction believed?" — meaning where the owner of the wine contradicts him, for he does not stand except for an oath (and such appears explicitly in the Ran in chapter 2 of Ketubot s.v. terveyhu, and in the responsum of Maharik root 33, and in Terumat HaDeshen siman 212, and other poskim — such is their explanation, and I proved so in my chiddushim on Kiddushin, not like what is written in Rashi's explanation: "and is it reasonable — one witness in contradiction, where one witness contradicts him — is the contradicted witness believed?"; I later found in the responsum of Maharam Padua siman 32 that he wrote there are variant texts in Rashi's language on this — see there); "and here even not in his presence," etc., means: since we find that one witness contradicting the owner of the wine is nothing because one witness stands only for an oath — if so, here too even not in his presence, since the owner of the wine contradicts him, this one cannot forbid his own, for one witness stands only for an oath; but where the owner of the wine is not before us and one witness contradicts him — Rashba does not discuss this at all; and on the contrary it appears somewhat from there that he holds that whoever the witness contradicts and says "it was not impure," the witness who says "it was impure" is not believed — see there in what is written; and although there is an answer to his words — "one contradicting witness is nothing" — examine if we do not say there is a textual error in the responsum, as is somewhat proven there; and examine further; and another great astonishment: even if you say Rashba holds the contradicting witness is nothing, this is only according to his view that I brought in s.k. 15, that he holds even "in your presence," even when he does not know, he is believed; but according to what the rabbi ruled, that the witness who says "it was libated" is never believed except through the silence of the owner of the wine, which is like admission, and it must be "in your presence" or "you knew circumstantial evidence" — if so, when the owner of the wine is not before us, even without the contradicting witness, the witness who says "it was libated" is not believed at all; and this is clear, and so it is proven in Or Zarua general law 13 din 13 explicitly, where he wrote there: but if the owner of the wine was not there, etc., anyone can contradict him, etc., as is below — end of his words; and it must mean in what is written "as is below" in what is written there that it must specifically be "in your presence"; and requires investigation; and it is also astonishing according to Pri Chadash's explanation, that he explained the reason because the words of one are not in place of two — why should the witness who says "it was not libated" not also be counted as two? For since Chazal believed this one who says "it was libated," who removes from the presumption of permit — all the more they believed this one who says "it was not libated"; and everywhere we do not say the words of one are not in place of two except where he is believed like two and not the other, such as regarding one witness says died and one witness says did not die in chapter 2 of Ketubot — for they believed this one who says died like two, for a matter of prohibition is not less than two, and they believed the one who says died because of the stringency imposed upon her at the end, as is in the first chapter of HaIsha Rabba; and similarly in several places; not so here; therefore one must say that what the rabbi wrote "and some wrote that one witness in contradiction is nothing" refers to the beginning, even when the owners are present and silent — since one witness contradicts and says "it was not libated," this one who says "it was libated" is one witness in contradiction and is nothing; and it appears to the rabbi thus from Rashba's silence, and since he wrote "one witness in contradiction is nothing," it implies he rules generally that one witness is never believed except in general, but in contradiction always nothing, even if the owners are silent; and the language "one witness in contradiction" is thus precise — the contradicted witness is nothing; and likewise in the language of the Ran in chapter 2 of Ketubot s.v. terveyhu, etc.; and in the language of the Ramban that the Hagid brought in chapter 12 of Hilchot Gerushin din 19, and other poskim — this language too is found, "one witness in contradiction is nothing," and its explanation there is that the contradicted witness is nothing — see there; and this is why the rabbi elaborated and wrote "and some wrote that one witness in contradiction is nothing," and did not write briefly "and some disagree," or "some say" one witness, etc., or "some say" it only helps — rather he means: and some wrote simply that one witness in contradiction is nothing, and there is in his language that always it is nothing, even if the owner of the wine is silent; and so from what the Ran wrote in chapter 2 of Ketubot there regarding one witness says she was betrothed and one witness says she was not betrothed, and she is silent, and this is not a proper time, etc.; and further, since one witness in contradiction — why should she not marry? Behold one witness in contradiction is nothing — end of his words; it is proven that the contradicted witness is never nothing, even if the owner of the wine is silent; and examine; and one should not challenge that if so in Keritot, one witness says he ate and one witness says he did not eat, who brings a conditional guilt offering to exempt completely — one may say chelev is different, for even if his heart tells him he brings a conditional guilt offering; and such is in the Yerushalmi in the first chapter of HaIsha Rabba, halacha 4: two say she was betrothed and two say she was not betrothed — R. Yona compared it to chelev: these two say so-and-so ate forbidden fat and two say he did not eat — he brings a conditional guilt offering from doubt; and here she should be given a bill of divorce from doubt; R. Yosei said to him: do not compare it to chelev, for there even if he said "my heart tells me" he brings a conditional guilt offering — examine; conclusion from this: where one witness says "your wine was libated" and one witness contradicts him and the owner of the wine is there and silent — for Semak and Or Zarua the wine is forbidden from doubt, and also for the contradicting witness it is forbidden l'chatchila; and for the Ran, that one witness in contradiction is nothing, the wine is kosher; and so the view of Rashba appears somewhat; and where the owners are not present — according to the Tur and his supporters, who require that he say specifically "it was libated in your presence" or "you knew circumstantial evidence" — it is obvious that even without the witness who contradicts him he is not believed to say "it was libated," since the owner of the wine is not before us for silence to be like admission; and it is possible that here all permit, since one witness contradicts him; and nevertheless this law, whether for Semak and Or Zarua or for Rashba and the Ran, is permitted; and examine; and further there is here a great reasoning to permit, because one may say: establish man against man and establish the wine in its original presumption of permit; and such is the view of Tosafot in chapter 2 of Ketubot (daf 23 side 1) s.v. terveyhu: one witness says she was betrothed and one witness says she was not betrothed — she may marry even l'chatchila, because we establish man against man and establish the woman in the presumption of being unmarried; all the more here regarding stam yeinam; however all this is when the two witnesses came at once; but one after another, since the first witness's testimony was already accepted in court and judgment was rendered on the basis of his testimony (as is written below), it is like two witnesses; and when afterward one witness comes to contradict him, the words of one are not in place of two — so Tosafot in chapter 2 of Ketubot (daf 22 side 2 s.v. im ken) and in the chapter HaIsha Shalom (Yevamot daf 117), and likewise Nimukei Yosef in the chapter HaIsha Shalom; and such is proven explicitly in the Gemara there; except that Nimukei Yosef in the first chapter of HaIsha Rabba wrote in the name of the Ritva, who wrote in the name of his teacher z"l: specifically testimony of a matter of prohibition, for we require two, and they believed this one who says died like two; but in a general prohibition where one suffices, since they did not believe him except as one, when another comes and contradicts him it is contradiction of one against one — end of his words; and after him Maharshal followed in the first chapter of Chullin siman 9, and Bach at the end of siman 1; and they ruled not like Maharik root 33, who ruled regarding one who said about the slaughterer that he slaughtered improperly and the slaughterer contradicts that the slaughter was valid — because since they believed the slaughterer it is like two, and the words of one are not in place of two; but the Mechaber at the end of siman 1 ruled like Maharik; and so it appears explicitly from the words of the Rosh in the chapter Nezikin and Mordechai in the chapter HaIsha Rabba in the explanation of fourteen distinctions in distinction 5; and likewise it appears in Tosafot in Keritot at the beginning of the chapter Amru Lo; and such is the view of the Rama that the Tur brought in Choshen Mishpat at the end of siman 66, that even in a matter that is not a matter of prohibition we say thus; and it appears to me there is proof for their words from the end of Sotah regarding one witness says I saw the killer and one says I did not see — we say there too: wherever the Torah believed one witness, behold he is like two, etc.; and it is possible to say that the view of the Ritva and his supporters is that certainly where Scripture revealed to us that one witness is believed, he is like two, for the Torah believed him like two; but where Scripture did not reveal to us except that it is reasonable or it is a rabbinic enactment that he is believed — such as a piece, doubt fat doubt milk, and one witness says it is fat; or where one witness told him "your wine was libated" and he is silent, and similarly; and everywhere we say one witness is believed in prohibitions — since Scripture did not reveal it to us, he is not considered like two; except that for woman's testimony, where by law two are required and Chazal believed one like two, the words of one are not in place of two; and there regarding the heifer whose neck is broken we derive from Scripture "it is not known" that one witness is believed, as is there; and according to this one may say the Rama agrees with the Ritva, that he speaks there regarding an oath, for Scripture revealed to us that he stands for an oath; however Maharik and his supporters do not disagree on this, that at once we do not say it is like two; and even though in the case of the slaughterer it is at once — it is different there, since they believed the slaughterer because of the presumption that most experts are found at slaughter — they assist him, as is in Maharik there; if so it is as if his testimony was already accepted in court — you will know, for otherwise it would be difficult on the rabbi, who wrote here divided opinions and at the end of siman 1 ruled like the Mechaber and Maharik; and examine; and this is also the reason that wherever one witness is believed from the Torah, even if one contradicts him immediately at once, his words are nothing, as Tosafot wrote in chapter 2 of Ketubot and in the chapter HaIsha Shalom there — because since the Torah believed one witness, it is as if his testimony was already accepted in court; and with this it appears clear to resolve what Tosafot wondered in the chapter Mi Shekinei from that which appears there in the Gemara regarding another witness who says she was defiled, that it is like two and the words of the one who says she was not defiled are nothing in place of two — from where do we say in HaIsha Shalom regarding one witness says died, specifically they permitted her on the basis of the court; and they entered with great difficulty, and even so Rashi and as appears from their words there did not resolve — see there; and according to what I wrote it is satisfactory, for that case in HaIsha Shalom is different, for the one witness who says died is not believed except rabbinically, specifically when he says before the court, for we hold a woman married on one witness not through the court must leave; and therefore as long as the court did not permit her, his testimony is not considered like two; but regarding sotah, the Merciful One believed one witness, as we derive from "if there was not in her," etc.; if so, immediately when he testified it is like two; such appears clear to me; and examine these laws well.
אע"ג דבלבו מאמין לו כבי תרי כו'. משמע דר"ל אע"ג שלבו נוקפו וברור לו שהעד אם לא היה יודע בירור הדבר לא היה אומר שנתנסך ומהימן לו בלבו כבי תרי מ"מ כיון שמוציא בשפתיו לומר איני מאמינך אין להחמיר וכן משמע בעט"ז ובאמת מוכח לכאורא במרדכי שהבין כן דברי ר"ת ע"ש אבל באמת נלפע"ד דלא עלה זה על דעת ר"ת דאם מאמינו בלבו כשנים שיאמר לו בפה איני מאמינך דודאי אם מאמינו בלבו כבי תרי ודמי ליה כאלו היה ב' אומרים נתנסך יינך איך יצא ידי שמים ויאמר איני מאמינך כב' אלא ר"ת ה"ק דאפילו אי מהימן ליה כב' יכול לומר איני מאמינך כלומר לדבר זה לא מהימנת לי כב' ואי א"ל הבע"ד הכי אמרינן ודאי קושטא קאמר דבלבו אינו מאמין לו כב' ולא נימא כיון דעד השתא מהימן ליה כב' שוב אין הבע"ד יכול לומר איני מאמינך דה"ל כאלו באו ב' עדים וא"ל נתנסך יינך אלא כיון דאמר איני מאמינך בטליה לנאמנותיה גם במרדכי יש לפרש כן ע"ש ודוק אע"פ שהוא דוחק קצת בל' ניחא לי טפי בהכי כדי שלא נאמר דס"ל לר"ת דאע"ג דמאמין לו בלבו כב' יבדה לומר איני מאמינך ולא נמצא שום מחבר שכ"כ בשם ר"ת או שיסבור כן ואף אם נאמר דס"ל לר"ת הכי מ"מ הא ר"מ בר"ק וראבי"ה חולקים והביאם המרדכי במסקנתו וכן נראה דעת התוס' בקדושין (דף ס"ה ע"ב) ד"ה נטמאו וכ"פ בהגהת מרדכי פ' המפקיד בשם ר' יעקב מקינו"ן ואע"ג דבסמ"ק ס"ס רנ"ג וכן באו"ה סוף כלל י"ג פסק כר"ת היינו משום שהבינו דעת ר"ת כמו שכתבתי דלא נמצא שם לישנא דמאמין לו בלבו ודוק גם הב"ח פסק לחומרא אף ביי"נ אם מאמין לו בלבו וע"ש: **** ENGLISH **** Even though in his heart he believes him like two, etc. It appears he means: even though his heart tells him and it is clear to him that the witness, if he did not know the matter clearly, would not have said it was libated, and he believes him in his heart like two witnesses — nevertheless, since he expresses with his lips "I do not believe you," one should not be stringent; and such appears in Pri Chadash; and in truth it appears at first glance in Mordechai that he understood Rabbenu Tam's words thus — see there; but in truth it appears to me that this did not enter Rabbenu Tam's mind, for if he believes him in his heart like two, how does he fulfill his obligation to Heaven and say with his mouth "I do not believe you"? For if he believes him in his heart like two, and it is like two saying "your wine was libated," how can he say "I do not believe you" like two? Rather Rabbenu Tam means: even if he believes him like two, he can say "I do not believe you" — meaning, for this matter you are not believed to me like two; and if the owner of the wine said so, we certainly say he speaks truth, for in his heart he does not believe him like two; and we should not say that since until now he believed him like two, the owner of the wine can no longer say "I do not believe you," for it is as if two witnesses came and told him "your wine was libated"; rather, since he said "I do not believe you," he nullified his credibility; and in Mordechai too one may explain thus — see there, and examine; even though it is somewhat forced in the language, it is preferable to me thus, so we do not say Rabbenu Tam holds that even though he believes him in his heart like two, he may come to say "I do not believe you"; and no author is found who wrote so in the name of Rabbenu Tam or who thinks so; and even if we say Rabbenu Tam holds thus — nevertheless R. Meir and Rabbenu Yehuda disagree, and Mordechai brought them in his conclusion; and such appears the view of Tosafot in Kiddushin (daf 65 side 2) s.v. nitmeu, and likewise in Hagahat Mordechai in the chapter HaMafkid in the name of R. Yaakov of Kinin; and even though Semak siman 253 and likewise Or Zarua at the end of general law 13 ruled like Rabbenu Tam — that is because they understood Rabbenu Tam's view as I wrote, for the language "believes him in his heart" is not found there; and examine; Bach too ruled stringently, even regarding stam yeinam, if he believes him in his heart — see there.

which he is silent because he does not know the matter clearly — that is the view of Tosafot, the Rosh, Mordechai, and Beit Yosef brings them; but one may be astonished, for behold the view of Rashba in responsum siman 376, and the Ran in the chapter HaOmer, and the Ritva, and Nimukei Yosef in the first chapter of HaIsha — that even if he did not tell him "in your presence" or "you knew," etc., but even if he is silent because he does not know the matter clearly, he is believed (and Beit Yosef did not bring them); and likewise the view of Raavan siman 64; and likewise it appears the view of the Raavad that Rashba brought in his chiddushim in the chapter Nezikin at the beginning of daf 39 — see there; and also R. Yerucham at the end of netiv 15, and the Rivash siman 245, wrote that there are disputants on Tosafot in this; and it is the view of the Acharonim that the Ran brought in the chapter HaOmer; and likewise Tosafot Rid agreed in Kiddushin daf 65 side 2 — see there; and it appears to me that this is the view of the Rambam, who wrote in chapter 9 of Hilchot Nezirut: if he was silent or was in doubt, he brings a sacrifice even on one witness; and in the Sifrei I wrote that such appears to me the main point from the Gemara in the chapter HaOmer (daf 66 side 1) from the blind man and Mina the king; and further from the first chapter of HaIsha Rabba, that the Gemara needs to say that one witness is believed in prohibitions even to remove a forbidden matter from its presumption of permit without silence like admission — it needs a source there; and it asks from where do we know; and it needs to derive from tevel and similar; and certainly there it is different because it is in his hand; and if so, although it was not resolved — nevertheless from where do we know for the other side that he is not believed? And if so, although for permit we hold stringently — nevertheless for issur perhaps he is believed, for certainly if he is believed to permit, all the more he is believed for issur; as the Rosh wrote in the chapter Nezikin, and Mordechai in the chapter HaIsha Rabba in fourteen distinctions — "all the more" is for issur than for permit; and further proof from the first chapter of Gittin (daf 2 side 2) and the first chapter of HaIsha Rabba, that it says there: say that we say one witness is believed in prohibitions — such as a piece, doubt milk doubt fat, that forbidden matter was not established; but here forbidden matter was established, for a woman is prohibited, not less than two — examine; and from that it mentions "it is a matter of prohibition," etc., and did not mention briefly "but here forbidden matter was established — no"; and further — examine; one must say as Tosafot wrote there in the name of R. Yitzchak, and Rashba in his chiddushim there, that in HaIsha Rabba regarding other prohibitions we are in doubt whether he is believed even when forbidden matter was established and not in his hand; and it says it is a matter of prohibition — that even for permit it remains in doubt, all the more for issur; and further, that below siman 141 Beit Yosef brought on daf 243 at the end of side 3 Rashbatz on a mikveh that was filled and we do not know if it was filled properly or not — that if we know who filled it, we ask his mouth, for one witness is believed in prohibitions even where forbidden matter was established, and even where it is not in his hand to fix, as is in Chullin and Gittin and several places — end of his words; behold he holds he is believed to permit, and all the more to forbid; and even though the rabbi there at the end of seif 4 wrote he is not believed except where it is in his hand to fix it, and that is from the words of Maharik root 15 — one may say that is because we are in doubt and go stringently; and if so, here he is believed from doubt stringently; and further it appears to me proof from what we say in Keritot in the first chapter Amru Lo: it teaches — they told him, "you ate forbidden fat," he brings a sin offering; they said, "how many were there?" — two; and what did he tell them? If we say he was silent and did not contradict them, but on silence of two he brings a sin offering — on silence of one I do not say the intermediate position: one witness says he ate and he says "I did not eat" — he is exempt; the reason is he contradicts him; but silence obligates, etc.; and if so, why does it challenge? And it answers there in a strained version: say the beginning that he is exempt is when they did not tell him "you should have known"; and further, why does it challenge from the intermediate position — let it challenge from the beginning: one witness says he ate and one witness says he did not eat — he brings a conditional guilt offering; the reason is one witness says he did not eat — otherwise he would be liable; it must deal with silence, for if he contradicts it is obvious he is exempt; and what Tosafot wrote there — likewise it could challenge from the beginning — is not so clear that this is a passage to challenge the beginning against the intermediate and not challenge from the beginning itself; rather certainly from the beginning it asks: one may say that that which he was silent he is liable is when they told him "you should have known," as Tosafot wrote in the chapter HaOmer; but from the intermediate position it deduces the reason that he said "he did not" — he contradicts explicitly; behold he was silent — no; even if it is not because of admission, nevertheless since he does not contradict him, he is believed — see there, and examine; however the view of Semak siman 223 and 205, and Hagahat Maimoni chapter 1 law 41, and R. Yerucham at the end of netiv 15, and in Agudah, and Or Zarua at the end of general law 23 — like the Tur; however certainly in practice Rashba and his supporters agree that if it is not in his hand and he did not tell him the first time he found it, he is not believed if the owner of the wine is not silent due to admission, as is proven in Nezikin; and they wrote the reason regarding a worker: since he accepted to do it properly, he is presumed to be very careful, and therefore he is not believed; and see in s.k. 3 and s.k. 8.
ואח"כ הכחישו. נ"ל דוקא אם מכחישו אח"כ אבל אם אמר ליה אח"כ איני יודע ומה ששתקתי תחלה לא מפני שהודיתי כו' העד נאמן לכ"ע והכי מוכח להדיא מן הש"ס) מעובדא דינאי מלכא בקידושין (דף ס"ו ע"א) ע"ש ודוק:
מה ששתקתי כו' אלא להתיישב כו'. כ"כ ג"כ רבינו ירוחם סוף נט"ו מיהו בנכ"ג חלק ב' כ' דאם א"ל בפניך נתנסך ושותק ואח"כ חזר ואמר לא שתקתי אלא מפני שלא חששתי לדברי העד לא מהני כיון דעד אחד נאמן באיסורים אבל בדבר שבערוה דאין פחות מב' אם אמר שתקתי מפני שלא חששתי לדברי העד מהני ע"כ דבריו בתוספת ביאור: **** ENGLISH **** What I was silent, etc., but to settle, etc. Rabbeinu Yerucham likewise wrote so at the end of netiv 15; however in the second part of Netiv 15 he wrote that if he told him "it was libated in your presence" and he is silent, and afterward he returned and said "I was not silent except because I did not care about the witness's words" — it does not help, since one witness is believed in prohibitions; but in a matter of prohibition where not less than two are required, if he said "I was silent because I did not care about the witness's words" — it helps; examine — his words are additional explanation.
יש מי שאומר כו' נאמן. ולעיל בסוף סי' א' סי"ג כתב המחבר בסתם שהוא נאמן וסתם הרב כותיה וכאן כתבו הרב בלשון יש מי שאומר משום שכתב ע"ז בד"מ וצריך לדקדק בסי' קפ"ה מנדה דלובשת בגדי נדה דלא מהני אמתלא ואולי יש לחלק וצ"ט עכ"ל וע"ל סימן קפ"ה ס"ק ה' דלדברי הב"ח והרב בתשובה מיושב זה שפיר עיין שם:
וכל הפסולי עדות כו'. דין זה כתוב בד"מ בשם הר"ן וכן נרשם בש"ע וצ"ע דהר"ן בקדושין פרק האומר כתב בהדיא דפסולי עדות אינן נאמנין באיסורין ובתשובה סימן כ"ה פסק דאפילו חשוד לאותו דבר כשר להעיד בשל אחרים כגון להשביח מקחו הוא לאו דוקא אלא ה"ה בכל מקום שיש למצא שום אמתלא וכן משמע בתשו' מהרי"ל ר"ס ל"ח וכן משמע בש"ס פרק בתרא דיבמות אי נמי דוקא התם צריך להאי טעמא כיון דהפירות שלו הן וכן משמע בת"ח כלל ל"ב ד"ט שוב מצאתי כן בתשו' הרשב"א סי' קי"ח להדיא ע"ש והשתא א"ש הא דמייתי ראיה מהך דיבמות דהם דברי רשב"ג ורבי הא פליג עליה בתוספתא דנאמן להחמיר ולא להקל וקי"ל הלכה כר' מחבירו (מיהו במרדכי פ' אלו מגלחין ובהגמ"י פ"ו מהל' אבל הביאו התוספתא דברי ר' רשב"ג אומר נאמן העובד כוכבים להחמיר כו' מיהו מבואר שם בדבריהם דקי"ל כרשב"ג דנאמן העובד כוכבים כו' ע"ש. וע"ל סי' ט"ז ס"ק כ"ג) אלא ודאי כדכתב הרא"ש פרק אלו מגלחין בשם מהר"מ דע"כ לא פליג ר' אלא כיון דפירות שלו הן אבל בעלמא מודה לרשב"ג וכן מוכח התם בהרא"ש דלרשב"ג ס"ל דבעלמא אינו נאמן אפילו בלא טעמא דלא נתכוין אלא להשביח מקחו דלא כדעת מהרש"ל שהבאתי לעיל סי' קכ"ב בס"ק (ג') [ד'] ונקוט האי כללא בידך דלעולם סלק עדותו של עובד כוכבים כמאן דליתיה ואין דבריו מעלין או מורידין בשל אחרים והכי אמרינן לקמן סי' ק"ץ ס"ק (נ"ו) [ס"ג] ומיהו היכא דמסיח לפי תומו כבר נתבאר דינו בסימן צ"ח ס"ק ב' וסימן שי"ג ס"ק ד': **** ENGLISH **** And all those invalid for testimony, etc. This law is written in Darkei Moshe in the name of the Ran, and likewise it was written in Shulchan Aruch; and requires investigation, for the Ran in Kiddushin in the chapter HaOmer wrote explicitly that those invalid for testimony are not believed in prohibitions; and in responsum siman 25 he ruled that even one who is suspect regarding that matter is fit to testify regarding others — such as to say this meat was slaughtered properly, and similarly; and it appears one should distinguish: to permit, certainly he is believed to testify, for we hold one who is suspect regarding a matter testifies for him, as above siman 119 s.k. 18; but in the chapter HaOmer he deals explicitly with coming to forbid another's — such as to say "your wine was libated" — then he is not believed except through the silence of the owner of the wine, who relies on the words of the fit witness, as the Ran wrote there; and therefore, whoever is invalid does not rely on him, and it is not enough in his regard to forbid another's; nevertheless for the rabbi it is difficult, for behold he speaks now regarding "your wine was libated," and according to the Ran those invalid for testimony are not believed; and even if you say he deals with testifying to permit — it is difficult, for in such a case the Ran holds that even one who is suspect is believed, and such we hold above siman 119 seif 7 and siman 124 seif 9; and requires investigation; I returned and examined Darkei Moshe, and such is its language: Rashba wrote in responsum siman 264 that two brothers are only like one witness for prohibitions, whether to uphold a matter or regarding contradiction; further the Ran wrote siman 350 that even one unfit for monetary testimony is believed to testify in prohibitions if he is not suspect regarding that matter — end of his words; and it appears this "further the Ran wrote" is a textual error, for if so it is not relevant to say siman 350; and further, if so it should have said "the Ran wrote," what is "further wrote"? Rather one must say: further Rashba wrote, for Rashba wrote so in responsum siman 350: all those invalid for testimony are fit in prohibitions, and even an apostate for one matter is fit for another matter that is not that matter — until here is his language — see there; and not as written in Shulchan Aruch "Ran" (and in Rashba too it appears there he deals with testifying to permit; but when testifying to forbid it appears he agrees with the Ran that those invalid for testimony are not believed, as appears in the Gemara in the chapter HaOmer (daf 66 side 1), and as written in s.k. 9 in the name of Tosafot and Mordechai, and likewise in the responsum of Rashba at the end of siman 376); and nevertheless requires investigation, for it appears Rashba in responsum siman 350 deals specifically with an apostate — meaning one who is a habitual offender; but regarding one who is suspect, behold he wrote in responsum siman 64 that even one suspect regarding that matter is believed to testify regarding others; and likewise above siman 2 s.k. 20 in the name of Turat Chaim and Kessef Mishneh, to distinguish between apostate and suspect — see there; and one may resolve that the rabbi too, when he says "unless he is suspect regarding that matter," speaks of an apostate regarding that matter; and in siman 119 seif 7 he deals with suspect and not apostate; and even though there he says "one who is well known for a transgression" — meaning he is well known to have done the transgression once, which makes him suspect and not a habitual offender to be an apostate; however in siman 124 seif 9 regarding coerced persons, they are certainly habitual offenders; and it is possible that since they do so out of coercion and pressure, we judge them as suspect; and examine. And regarding the testimony of gentiles — poskim wrote in several places that gentiles are not believed, neither for issur nor for heter; and see above siman 118 s.k. 37, and siman 122 s.k. 3, and at the end of siman 129, and siman 130 at the end of seif 8 in the hagahah; and it appears that even if he has no benefit in his testimony, he is not believed to testify regarding others; and even though Semag negative commandment 137 on daf 41 at the end of side 2 wrote in the name of Rav Hai Gaon that we do not rely on the words of a gentile, neither for issur nor for heter — for issur, from what we say in the last chapter of Yevamot: a gentile who was selling produce in the market and said "these fruits are orlah," "these are tithed" — he said nothing; he did not intend this except to improve his sale, etc. — end of his words; it is not to say that specifically where he has benefit in his testimony, such as there where he intends to improve his sale, but generally he is believed to forbid; for the principle is always applied that we never rely on gentiles; rather the reason that he did not intend except to improve his sale is not precise, but the same applies everywhere one can find some excuse; and such appears in the responsum of Maharil siman 38; and likewise it appears in the Gemara in the last chapter of Yevamot; or also specifically there this reason is needed, since the produce is his; and likewise it appears in Turat Chaim general law 32 din 9; I later found likewise in the responsum of Rashba siman 118 explicitly — see there; and now one may ask on the proof from that passage in Yevamot, for they are the words of Rashbag and Rabbi — behold the Tosafeta disagrees, that a gentile is believed to be stringent and not to be lenient, and we hold the halacha is like Rabbi over his colleague (however in Mordechai in the chapter Elu Megalchin, and in Hagahat Maimoni chapter 6 of Hilchot Avodah Zarah, they brought the Tosafeta — the words of Rabbi: Rashbag says a gentile is believed to be stringent, etc.; however it is explained there in their words that we hold like Rashbag, that a gentile is believed, etc. — see there; and see above siman 16 s.k. 23); rather certainly, as the Rosh wrote in the chapter Elu Megalchin in the name of Maharam: Rabbi only disagrees because the produce is his; but generally he agrees with Rashbag; and such is proven there in the Rosh, that for Rashbag he holds that generally he is not believed, even without the reason that he did not intend except to improve his sale — not like the view of Maharshal that I brought above siman 122 in s.k. 4; and take this principle in your hand, that we always dismiss the testimony of a gentile as though he does not exist, and his words do not raise or lower regarding others; and such we say below siman 139 s.k. 63; however where he speaks innocently, his law was already explained in siman 98 s.k. 2 and siman 313 s.k. 4.

If it is in his hand. The language of the Tur: such as when it was given into his hand to guard it; and he means that “in his hand” does not mean in his hand to libate it, but rather that it was given into his hand to guard it, and it is as if he were its owner over it; and not because of a migu; and so ruled the Rosh in the chapter Nezikin in distinction 11, and Mordechai at the beginning of the chapter HaIsha Rabba; but Beit Yosef did not bring the words of the Rosh and Mordechai, and on the contrary brought simply the words of Rashi, Rabbenu Tam, and the Rashba, who explained: anyone within whose hand it is to defile it; and perhaps for this reason he omitted the language of the Tur here; and likewise in Pri Chadash he explained the reason because it is within his power to diminish it; and the Rashba proved it in his chiddushim in the chapter Nezikin at the beginning of daf 79 with proofs; and it is implied in Tosafot in Kiddushin in the chapter HaOmer (daf 65 side 2) that he is believed because of a migu; and according to this one may consider: one who says to his fellow regarding his boiled wine that it was libated before the boiling is not believed) even if it is in his hand, since he has no migu.
Believed. Even if he did not tell him the first time he found it.
But if it is not in his hand. Meaning: even if it was in his hand initially, nevertheless since it is not now in his hand and he did not tell him the first time, he is not believed; but when it was never in his hand at all, even if he told him the first time, he is not believed when the owner of the wine contradicts him — except when he is silent; so it is explained in Tosafot, the Rosh, Mordechai, and their supporters; and the Mechaber abbreviated the matter.
If the owner contradicts him. And then it is permitted for everyone; and so too the rabbi wrote at the end of the seif; and even if he said “I do not know,” it is permitted for everyone — as written in Or Zarua general law 13 din 13 in the name of R. Chaim; and so too ruled Darkei Moshe.
Or he says, etc. It is written in Mordechai in the chapter HaOmer that if he says to him "perhaps you were not careful," it is considered as if he contradicts him; and Darkei Moshe brings it.
Does not know. See above s.k. 15.
And they teach him, etc. Meaning: they teach him before the witness tells him, that when the witness comes and says to him, he should say to him immediately within the time of speech "I do not believe you"; and they do not teach him to contradict him, for how would they teach him to lie.
And afterward he contradicted him. It appears to me specifically if he contradicts him afterward; but if he told him afterward "I do not know, and that I was silent at first was not because I admitted," etc. — the witness is believed according to all; and this is proven explicitly from the Gemara, from the incident of King Yannai in Kiddushin (daf 66 side 1) — see there and examine.
Some say, etc., he is believed. And above at the end of siman 1, seif 13, the Mechaber wrote simply that he is believed, and the rabbi ruled likewise; and here the rabbi wrote it in the language of “some say” because he wrote concerning it in Darkei Moshe: one must examine in siman 185 regarding a niddah who wears niddah garments, that an excuse does not help — and perhaps one may distinguish; and requires investigation — end of his words; and see above siman 185 s.k. 5, that according to Bach and the rabbi in responsum, this is resolved nicely — see there.

turei_zahav.he:
אבל בשאר איסורים לא מהני כו'. כי יש חולקין וס"ל דכל שהוא מאמין בלבו שאומר אמת אין מועיל מה שמכחישו ועל זה נאמר ויראת מאלהיך:
אלא להתיישב ולחשוב בלבי כו'. משמע לי באם לא אמר כך אלא אמר שתקתי שהייתי סבור כיון שאני איני יודע ואתה יודע בבירור ועכשיו שמעתי מאחרים שאינך נאמן ומברר זה מאותן אחרים שהגידו לו כן דנאמן הוא בכך וכאלו אמר מתחלה איני יודע וראייה לזה מח"מ סימן כ' שהביא רמ"א שאם הביא ראיה שלא ידע תחילה מאלו עדים כו' וה"נ דכוותיה אבל אם אמר תחלה שתקתי שלא חשתי להשיבך אינו נאמן אע"פ שבח"מ סי' פ"א מצינו שיכול לומר כן לענין הודאות ממון שאני התם דיכול לומר אני ידעתי האמת שלא יזיק לי דבריך שאתה אומר שיש לך מנה בידי כיון שאין אני מוציא מפי שום דבר אבל כאן אין אדם עשוי שלא לחוש אם אומרים שהוא שותה איסור וע"פ דרך זה נ"ל ליישב מה שכתב ב"י בשם הרשב"א הא דמחלקינן כאן בין פעם הא' או לא דוקא בפועל או שומר אבל עד דעלמא נאמן אפילו לא אמר ליה בפעם הראשון שמצאו שמא לא נזכר בפעם הראשון דלאו עליה רמיא או שלא רצה להעיד לו ולבתר כן נמלך ואמר ליה עכ"ל. והקשה עליו בד"מ דע"כ הא דעד דעלמא נאמן היינו כשבעלים שותקין ואם כן פשיטא שאין לחלק בין פעם הראשון לפעם השני דמ"מ שתיקתו כהודאה בשלמא בשומר יש לחלק שפיר דפעם הראשון הוי שומר שלא במקצת ולא בפעם השני אבל במקום שהאיסור משום שתיקת הבעלים מה לי פעם הראשון ומה לי פעם שני עכ"ל ולי נראה דלא קשה מידי דהוי אמינא שיכול הבעל לומר כיון שכבר ראית אותי ולא אמרת לי דבר לאפרושי מאיסורא ועכשיו אתה אומר לי אין זה אלא דרך שחוק והיתול ועל כן לא חששתי להשיבך קמ"ל דלא אמרינן כן אלא נאמן אף בזה כיון שהוא אינו שומר שלו ובאמת רבותא גדולה היא:
טבח שעשה סי' בו'. בסי' א' סעיף י"ג כתבתי שאין לפסוק כן וכאן מצאתי בד"מ שגם הוא הקשה כן וכתב בסוף ואולי יש לחלק וצ"ע עכ"ל:
turei_zahav.en:
But with regard to other prohibitions, this is ineffective, etc. For there are those who disagree and hold that whenever he believes in his heart that the other person is speaking truthfully, his verbal denial is ineffective. Concerning this it is stated, “You shall fear your God.”
Rather, I remained silent in order to collect my thoughts and consider the matter, etc. It appears to me that if he did not say this, but instead said, “I remained silent because I thought that, since I do not know and you know with certainty, I should accept your words; but now I have heard from others that you are not trustworthy,” and he substantiates this through those others who told him so, he is believed through this claim. It is as though he had said from the outset, “I do not know.” A proof for this may be brought from Choshen Mishpat siman 20, where the Rama states that if one brings proof that he was initially unaware of these witnesses, etc., he is believed; the same applies here. But if he initially said, “I remained silent because I did not consider it worthwhile to answer you,” he is not believed. Although in Choshen Mishpat siman 81 we find that one may make such a claim regarding admissions concerning money, that case is different, for he can say, “I knew the truth, that your statement that I owe you 100 would not harm me, since I did not utter anything myself.” Here, however, a person does not ordinarily remain unconcerned when he is told that he is consuming a prohibited substance. Based on this approach, it appears to me that one can resolve what the Beit Yosef wrote in the name of the Rashba. The distinction made here between whether the person told him the first time or not applies specifically to a worker or a custodian. An ordinary witness, however, is believed even if he did not tell him the first time he encountered him, for perhaps he did not remember the matter the first time, since responsibility for it did not rest upon him, or perhaps he did not wish to testify to him then and afterward reconsidered and told him, end quote. The Darkei Moshe challenged this: Necessarily, the ordinary witness is believed only where the owner remains silent. If so, it is obvious that there is no distinction between the first time and the second time, for in either case the owner's silence is equivalent to an admission. Granted, with a custodian one can properly distinguish, for at the first encounter he was the custodian, whereas later he was not; but where the prohibition arises because of the owner's silence, what difference is there between the first time and the second time? End quote. It appears to me, however, that there is no difficulty at all. One might have thought that the owner can say, “Since you had already seen me and did not tell me anything to separate me from a prohibition, and now you suddenly tell me, I regarded your words merely as jest and mockery, and therefore I did not trouble myself to answer you.” The Rashba therefore teaches that we do not say this. Rather, the witness is believed even in such a case, since he was not the owner's custodian. This is indeed a significant novelty.
A slaughterer who made a sign upon it, etc. In siman 1, seif 13, I wrote that one should not rule this way. Here I found that the Darkei Moshe likewise raised this difficulty and concluded, “Perhaps a distinction may be drawn, but the matter requires further study,” end quote.

baer_heitev.he:
נאמן. כתב הש"ך ואפילו לא אמר לו בפעם הראשון שמצאו והטעם דנאמן משום מגו דבידו לנסכו וע"פ זה יש לדון במי שאומר לחבירו על (*) [אבל ז"א דע"כ מיירי כאן בגוונא דלא מקרי הפ"מ דאם לא כן למה צריך ס' נגד הקילוח]. יין מבושל שלו שנתנסך קודם הבשול אינו נאמן אפילו הוא בידו כיון דלית ליה מגו עד כאן לשונו:
מכחישו. והש"ך חולק על זה וס"ל דדוקא אם הבעלים שותקים הוא נאמן אבל אם הבעלים מכחישים אותו אינו נאמן כדאי' בח"מ סי' ק"ח סי"ד וכ' הר"ב בתשובה סי' ס"ו דאם הבעל מכחישו בזה שלא א"ל בפעם הראשון שמצאו ודאי הבעל נאמן ע"ש:
אינו. ואז מותר לכל העולם דאפילו אמר איני יודע מותר לכל העולם כ"כ בד"מ וכ' המרדכי דאם א"ל שמא לא דקדקת חשוב כאילו הכחישו:
כהודאה. פי' אפילו אמר שלא היה בידו מעולם ולא א"ל בפעם הא' לעולם כיון דשתיקה כהודאה דמיא ואין חילוק בין פועל לשומר בין א"ל מיד או לא הוי שתיקה כהודאה ולאו כהודאה ממש אלא כיון ששותק נראה שיודע רגלים לדבר וסומך על העד כ"כ התוס' עכ"ל הש"ך:
ומלמדים. פי' מלמדים אותו קודם שא"ל העד שכשיבא העד ויאמר לו יאמר לו מיד תוך כדי דיבור איני מאמינך ואין מלמדים אותו להכחישו דהיאך ילמדוהו לשקר (ובנה"כ פי' דמלמדין אותו לומר איני יודע ע"ש):
אחר. והש"ך חולק ע"ז ופסק דמ"מ איסורא איכא לכתחלה אבל בדיעבד אין להחמיר להעד עצמו:
מהני. כתב הש"ך הל' קשה דמאי מהני הא אפילו לא יכחיש אין עדותו כלום כיון דאין הבע"ד לפנינו דהא צ"ל בפניך או ידעת כו' וי"ל דמהני הכחשתו דאפי' אומר אחר כך גם כן בפני הבע"ד ושותק אינו נאמן דכיון דטעמא דשתיקה וכו' דסומך על דברי העד כמ"ש לעיל הילכך אי איתכחיש כבר תו לא סמיך עליה וצ"ע לדינא עד כאן לשונו (ובנה"כ מתרץ דהא דכתב המחבר דצריך לומר בפניך וכו' מיירי דוקא כשהבעלים בכאן רק לענין שתיקה כהודאה בזה קאמר דצ"ל בפניך משא"כ אם הבעלים מתו או הלכו למה"י ועד א' אומר שיין זה נתנסך ולית מאן דמכחיש ליה פשיטא דנאמן לזה כתב דאם אחר מכחישו האחר נאמן ע"ש):
תרי. כתב הש"ך דזה תמוה אם נאמן לו כבי תרי היאך יוצא ידי שמים ויאמר איני מאמינך אלא ה"ק דאפילו אי מהימן ליה כתרי יכול לומר איני מאמינך כלומר לדבר זה לא מהימנת לי כבי תרי ואי א"ל הבע"ד הכי אמרינן ודאי קושטא קאמר דבלבו אינו מאמין לו כב' ולא נימא כיון דעד השתא מהימן ליה כב' שוב אין הבע"ד יכול לומר איני מאמינך דה"ל כאלו באו ב' עדים וא"ל נתנסך יינך אלא כיון דא"ל איני מאמינך בטליה לנאמנותיה אע"פ שהוא דוחק קצת בלשון ניחא לי טפי בהכי כדי שלא נאמר דס"ל לר"ת דאע"ג דמאמין ליה בלבו כב' יבדה לומר איני מאמינך ולא נמצא שום מחבר שכ"כ בשם ר"ת או שיסבור כן אלא שצ"ע דמשמע דלדעה זו אפי' אין הבע"ד שם עד זה המכחיש ואומר לא נתנסך לאו כלום הוא וכן פי' העט"ז ודין זה הוא תמוה וחולק הש"ך ע"ז ופסק כשאין הבע"ד לפנינו אפי' בלא עד המכחיש אין העד שאומר נתנסך נאמן כלל ומכ"ש אם האחר מכחישו דשרי לכ"ע (וכבר כתבתי לעיל בס"ק ז' דבנה"ך חזר בו ולכך פי' דהאי ויש מי שכתב קאי אם הבעלים לפנינו ושתקו ויש כאן עד א' המכחיש עד הנכחש לאו כלום הוא) מיהו כל זה כשבאו הב' עדים בבת אחת אבל בזה אחר זה כיון שכבר נתקבל עדות הא' בב"ד ונפסק הדין על פי עדותו הוה ליה כב' עדים וכשבא אח"כ עד אחד להכחישו אין דבריו של א' במקום שנים וע"ל סי' א' מה שפסק המחבר גבי שוחט ששחט שלא כהוגן והשוחט מכחיש שהשחיטה כשרה וכו' מיהו היכא דבאו בבת א' לא אמרינן דראשון ה"ל כב' ואע"ג דבעובדא דהשוחט הוי בבת אחת שאני התם כיון דהאמינוהו להשוחט משום דרוב מצוין אצל שחיטה מומחין הם ה"ל כאלו נתקבל עדותו כבר וכן בכ"מ היכא דגלי לן קרא דעד אחד נאמן ה"ל כב' דהא התורה האמינתו כב' אבל היכא דלא גלי קרא אלא דמסברא או מתקנת חכמים הוא נאמן כגון חתיכה ספק שומן ספק חלב וע"א אמר דהוא שומן או היכא דאמר ליה עד א' נתנסך יינך והוא שותק וכה"ג ובכל דוכתא דאמרינן עד א' נאמן באיסורים כיון דלא גלי לן קרא לא חשיב כב' אלא דבעדות אשה הקילו והאמינו לחד כב' ואין דבריו של א' במקום שנים עכ"ל:
ידעת. כתב הש"ך דאל"ה לא הוי שתיקה כהודאה דהא דשותק משום שאינו יודע בירור הדבר מיהו תימא שהרי כמה פוסקים פסקו דאף ששותק מחמת שאינו יודע בירור הדבר אפ"ה העד נאמן ומאריך עוד בכמה ראיות מש"ס ותוס' המוכיחין כך וסיים מיהו ודאי בפועל אף הרשב"א וסייעתו מודים דאם אינו בידו ולא אמר ליה בפעם הא' שמצאו אינו נאמן אם אין הבע"ד שותק מחמת הודאה וטעמא דפועל כיון שקיבל לעשותה בהכשר חזקה מיזהר זהיר ולכך אינו נאמן:
הכחישו. נ"ל דוקא אם מכחישו אחר כך אבל אם אמר ליה אחר כך איני יודע ומה ששתקתי תחלה לא מפני שהודיתי וכו' העד נאמן לכ"ע ש"ך וכתב רבינו ירוחם ואם אמר ליה בפניך נתנסך ושותק ואח"כ חזר ואמר לא שתקתי אלא מפני שלא חששתי לדברי העד לא מהני כיון דע"א נאמן באיסורים אבל בדבר שבערוה דאין פחות מב' אם אמר שתקתי מפני שלא חששתי לדברי העד מהני וכתב הט"ז וז"ל משמע לי אם אמר שתקתי שהייתי סבור כיון שאני איני יודע ואתה יודע בבירור ועכשיו שמעתי מאחרים שאינך נאמן ומברר זה מאותן אחרים שהגידו לו כן דנאמן הוא בכך וכאלו אמר מתחלה איני יודע וראיה לזה ממ"ש רמ"א בח"מ סי' כ' שאם הביא ראיה שלא ידע תחלה מאלו עדים וכו' וה"נ דכוותיה אבל אם אמר מה ששתקתי תחלה שלא חששתי להשיבך אינו נאמן ואפילו לא אמר ליה העד בפעם הא' ואין הבע"ד יכול לומר כיון שכבר ראית אותי ולא אמרת לי דבר לאפרושי מאיסורא ועכשיו אתה אומר לי אין זה אלא דרך שחוק והיתול וע"כ לא חששתי להשיבך דאין אדם עשוי שלא לחוש אם אומרים שהוא שותה איסור עכ"ל:
שאומר. כתב הש"ך ולעיל בס"ס א' סי"ג כ' המחבר בסתם שהוא נאמן וסתם הר"ב כוותיה וכאן כתב הר"ב בשם יש מי שאומר משום שכתב ע"ז בד"מ וצריך לדקדק בסי' קפ"ה מנדה דלובשת בגדי נדה דלא מהני אמתלא ואולי יש לחלק וצ"ע וגם הט"ז כ' בסי' א' דאין לפסוק כן ע"ש:
שחשוד. כ' הש"ך דוקא אם הוא מומר לאותו דבר אבל אם הוא רק חשוד כתב לעיל סי' קי"ט ס"ז דנאמן ואע"ג דקאמר התם מי שהוא מפורסם בעבירה היינו שהוא מפורסם שעשה העבירה פעם א' דהוי חשוד ואינו מועד להיות מומר מיהו בסימן קכ"ד ס"ט באנוסים ודאי מועדים הם ואפשר כיון דמתוך אונס ודחק עושים כן כחשודים דיינינן להו ולענין עדות העובד כוכבים כתבו הפוסקים דאינו נאמן לא לאיסור ולא להיתר ונראה דאפילו אין לו הנאה בעדותו אינו נאמן להעיד בשל אחרים מיהו היכא דמסל"ת כבר נתבאר דינו בסי' צ"ח ס"א וסי' שי"ג ס"ב בהג"ה עכ"ל:
baer_heitev.en:
Believed. Shach writes that he is believed even if he did not tell him the first time he encountered him, because he has a migo that he could have poured the wine for idolatrous use while it was in his control. Accordingly, one who says that another person's cooked wine had been libated before it was cooked is not believed even if the wine is presently in his possession, because he lacks that migo.
Contradicts him. Shach disagrees and holds that the witness is believed only when the owner is silent. If the owner contradicts him, he is not believed, as stated in Choshen Mishpat 108:14. Rama writes in a responsum that if the owner contradicts him by saying that the witness did not tell him this when he first encountered him, the owner is certainly believed.
Is not. It is then permitted to everyone. Darkei Moshe writes that even if the owner says, 'I do not know,' it is permitted to everyone. Mordechai writes that if he says, 'Perhaps you were not precise,' this is treated as a contradiction.
Like an admission. Even if the worker says the item was never in his control and he did not tell the owner the first time, silence is treated as admission. There is no distinction between a worker and a guardian, or between immediate and delayed reporting. It is not literally an admission; rather, his silence indicates that he recognizes grounds for the claim and relies upon the witness. Shach.
And they instruct him. Meaning, they instruct the owner before the witness speaks that when the witness arrives, he should immediately say within the time required for speech, 'I do not believe you.' They do not instruct him to contradict the witness factually, for they may not teach him to lie. Nekudot HaKesef explains that they instruct him to say, 'I do not know.'
Another. Shach disagrees and rules that there is still an initial prohibition, though after the fact one should not be stringent even for the witness himself.
Helps. Shach asks what the contradiction accomplishes, since if the owner is absent the testimony is ineffective in any case, because the witness must say, 'It was done in your presence,' or, 'You knew.' He answers that the contradiction helps even if the first witness later repeats his testimony before the owner and the owner remains silent. Since silence is effective because the owner relies upon the witness, once that witness has already been contradicted the owner no longer relies upon him. Nekudot HaKesef explains that the requirement to say, 'In your presence,' applies only when the owner is present and his silence is treated as admission. If the owners died or went overseas and one witness says that this wine was libated, he is ordinarily believed unless another witness contradicts him.
Like two. Shach explains that even if the owner generally trusts the witness like two witnesses, he may say, 'I do not believe you,' meaning that in this matter he does not trust him as two. Once he says this, we accept that he truly lacks such trust. If two witnesses arrive sequentially and the first testimony was already accepted by beit din and judgment rendered, the first is treated as two and a later single witness cannot contradict him. If they arrive together, the first is not treated as two. Where Scripture itself grants credibility to one witness, he is treated as two; where credibility arises only from reasoning or rabbinic enactment, as in ordinary prohibitions, he is not.
You knew. Shach writes that otherwise silence is not admission, because the owner may be silent simply because he does not know the facts. He notes, however, that many authorities hold that even such silence gives credibility to the witness. Regarding a worker, all agree that if the item is no longer in his control and he did not report the matter when he first encountered the owner, he is not believed unless the owner's silence reflects admission, because a worker who accepted responsibility to perform the task properly is presumed to have been careful.
Contradicted him. Shach explains that this means the owner later contradicts the witness. If he later says only, 'I do not know, and my earlier silence was not admission,' the witness remains believed according to all. Rabbeinu Yerucham writes that if the witness said, 'Your wine was libated in your presence,' and the owner was silent, he cannot later say that he ignored the witness, because one witness is believed in prohibitions. In matters of sexual prohibition, where two witnesses are required, such an explanation is effective. Taz writes that if the owner says he was silent because he thought the witness knew with certainty, but later heard from others, whom he identifies, that the witness is unreliable, he is believed, as though he initially said, 'I do not know.' But he is not believed to say that he merely did not care to answer, because a person does not ordinarily ignore a claim that he is consuming a prohibition.
Who says. Shach notes that above, at the end of siman 1, the Mechaber rules without qualification that such a person is believed, and Rama concurs. Here Rama cites the ruling as 'some say' because Darkei Moshe questioned it from siman 185, where a woman who wore niddah garments cannot later offer an excuse. Perhaps the cases differ, but the matter requires study. Taz also writes in siman 1 that one should not rule this way.
Suspected. Shach writes that this applies specifically to an apostate regarding that matter. One who is merely suspected remains believed, as stated in siman 119:7. A non-Jew is not believed either to prohibit or to permit, even where he has no personal benefit from his testimony. The law of a non-Jew speaking innocently was explained in siman 98:1 and siman 313:2 in the gloss.

beer_hagolah.he:
תוס' גיטין דף נ"ד ע"ב אאוקימתא דאביי שם:
כאוקימתא דרבא שם:

שם בשם ריצב"א:
beer_hagolah.en:
Tosafot, Gittin 54b, concerning Abaye's interpretation there.
In accordance with Rava's interpretation there.
Tosafot there proved this in the name of Rabbeinu Tam from the dispute between Abaye and Rava in Kiddushin 54b and from Yevamot 88a. Rosh likewise wrote this there.
